A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GADL research. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables, proofs, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial reformatting and added analyses.

before.justification: V1 reports original GADL results on graph and vision-language benchmarks, component ablations, encoder comparisons, and hyperparameter sensitivity experiments.

after.justification: V3 retains original benchmark experiments and adds latent-alignment visualizations, spectral-energy measurements, discriminability and oversmoothing analyses, and runtime results.

M1.justification: The core encoder equations, functional maps, decoder, losses, and greedy graph-matching procedure are unchanged. However, v3 Appendix C.5 newly specifies unshared vision-language encoders and Hungarian assignment, whereas v1 provides only the general shared-encoder/greedy description. The PDFs do not establish whether these are procedural revisions or previously undocumented exceptions.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same six semi-synthetic graphs, ACM-DBLP and Douban Online-Offline, and CIFAR-10, CINIC-10, CIFAR-100, and ImageNet-100. The synthetic illustration and pretrained-model coverage are retained. V3's new diagnostics reuse existing datasets and perturbation scenarios.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in Tables 1–3 and the retained encoder comparison are unchanged. V3 adds evaluated GCN + PairNorm and GCN + DropEdge controls in the oversmoothing experiment (Appendix H, Figure 7). Vec2Vec and CycleReward are discussed but explicitly not evaluated.

E3.justification: V3 introduces substantial diagnostic protocols: t-SNE visualization of 50 corresponding pairs, spectral-energy measurements, nearest-neighbor embedding discrimination, and MAD after L2 normalization across depths 1–8. Appendix I adds per-epoch timing, a one-hour timeout, and separate eigendecomposition timing. Existing perturbation levels and benchmark accuracy metrics remain unchanged; newly disclosed vision-language settings do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: V1's component ablation is retained and expanded in v3 Table 6 with low-pass-only, high-pass-only, and joint-regularizer-removal variants. V3 additionally examines latent-space consistency, learned spectral energy, node uniqueness, oversmoothing across depth, and computational efficiency. The earlier encoder and hyperparameter studies remain in Appendices F and J rather than being newly introduced.

E5.justification: V3 Appendix C.5 newly distinguishes baseline variability from sampling half the image embeddings versus GADL variability from initialization seeds using all embeddings. The existing reporting of standard deviations over 10 perturbed target graphs and 20 vision-language seeds is retained. No increase in those run counts is established.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises several GADL values, including Cora at 5% perturbation from 68.22 ± 0.2 to 71.12 ± 0.4. Table 3 replaces most GADL vision-language scores: CLIP ViT-L/14@336 with all-mpnet-base-v2 on CIFAR-100 changes from 79.7 ± 2.0 to 16.8 ± 4.1, below unchanged LocalCKA at 24.00 ± 1.41. Earlier appendix values remain in Table 9 as best-over-training results, so the replacements are not established same-protocol performance declines. New diagnostic, ablation, and timing results are also added; Table 2 is unchanged.

T1.justification: The central theorem and separation-margin claim are retained. Appendix B revises the neighborhood-preservation argument by introducing the explicit spectral-overlap product λ(2−λ)/4 instead of merely asserting expected orthogonality. New Appendix I supplies componentwise and overall asymptotic complexity derivations. These extend the mathematical discussion without replacing the central theorem.

C1.justification: The central unsupervised dual-pass/functional-map contribution remains. V3 emphasizes complementary filtering in feature and map spaces, removes vision-language generalization from the abstract and headline contribution list, and qualifies benchmark superiority in that list as occurring 'in most settings.' Vision-language applicability remains claimed in the conclusion.

C2.justification: V3 explains functional maps as indirect training constraints and distinguishes function-space bijectivity from node bijection. It adds interpretations of why embedding spread alone does not ensure alignment, why heterogeneous Douban graphs benefit from regularization, and where high-pass filtering or PairNorm can fail. It also qualifies retained appendix vision-language scores as optimistic best test accuracies over training and acknowledges limitations in large-scale ground truth and specialized vision-language comparisons.

D1.justification: V3 adds an implementation URL, explicit loss weights and selection guidance, and detailed vision-language configuration: five-neighbor graphs, four encoder layers, 512-dimensional hidden/output representations, and 9 or 90 eigenvectors. It newly documents modality-specific weight sharing and assignment choices, sampling differences, and preprocessing costs. These substantially expand the earlier hardware, optimizer, and graph-architecture disclosures without necessarily indicating implementation changes.

R1.justification: Appendix A adds focused positioning against GPR-GNN, BernNet, TFE-GNN, and FAGCN, distinguishing feature-space filtering from cross-graph map constraints. V3 also adds functional-map references, discusses Vec2Vec and CycleReward, and cites the new oversmoothing controls. The existing alignment taxonomy and most related-work discussion remain; publication updates for retained works are not new research coverage.

P1.justification: V3 rewrites the abstract and contribution list, condenses several methodological and results passages, moves the semi-synthetic setup and main component ablation into appendices, and reorganizes implementation subsections. The overall narrative and much existing exposition remain recognizable; much of the expansion consists of new scientific analyses rather than wholesale rewriting.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from single-column to two-column layout with extensive resizing and relocation of displays. V3 adds frequency-response, t-SNE, spectral-energy, and MAD-depth figures, new uniqueness and runtime tables, and additional ablation rows. Earlier encoder, sensitivity, and vision-language figures are retained as Figures 6, 8, and 9; the latter gains a best-over-training caption.

improvement.justification: V3 adds branch and joint-regularizer ablations missing from v1, documents essential implementation settings, and identifies retained vision-language appendix scores as optimistic best test accuracies over training. These improve empirical support and transparency. The net gain is limited by the unexplained selection of replacement Table 3 scores and the new runtime discussion's total-time claims without reported epoch budgets, alongside ambiguous greedy/Hungarian terminology.
